svg.aria-label: How the Rose Hobart booth works. You run the projector. On the picture side there are six presets, from As circulated and Cornell 1936 to Pink filter, Nitrate decay, Broken projector and Digital decay; six theatrical gels, including Cornell blue and pink, with a density slider; an Age dial that runs from fresh print to nitrate rot; and a Glitch dial that runs from clean to datamoshed. All of them feed one WebGL2 shader that repaints every frame of the film. Speed sets the video's playback rate, 16 frames a second as circulated or 24 at sound speed, and the pitch moves with it. Music swaps the film's 1957 records for eight 78s from 1919 to 1924, My Bloody Valentine's Soon, or silence, and a record only plays while the film runs. Without WebGL2 the film still plays as circulated, with speed and music.
